items.note: The whole temple is symbolic of the universe, with the eight Regents of the cardinal points on the walls and circumambulation as a perambulation of the universe; general interpretive background.
Architectural origins: base from the Vedic sacrificial altar, sanctum from the dolmen, spire from a bamboo tabernacle; shikhara represents a mountain (Meru, Mandara, Kailasa).
Sanctum has one front door and false doors as niches on the other three sides; main and lesser aspects of the deity placed in cardinal and minor niches.
River-goddesses on the doorframe and the tutelary symbol on the lintel, as the last carved member before the sanctum.
From about the 7th century the sanctum is roofed by a curvilinear shikhara of 3, 5 or occasionally 7 projections, ending in griva, amalasaraka and kalasha; general Northern-style background.
Socle of moulded courses, wall with figure-sculptures on offsets, eave-cornice separating wall from spire, and a lower pyramidal roof on the mandapa.
Construction: dressed ashlar face-stones, dry-laid courses with iron clamps and dowels, and hollow chambers inside tall spires.
A Bhagavata shrine at Besnagar near Sanchi, elliptical on plan and possibly of timber; in front stands the pillar of the Greek ambassador Heliodorus, who called himself a Bhagavata.
Temple 40 at Sanchi, a Maurya apsidal stone temple on a high socle with an ambulatory; superstructure possibly timber and lost.
The Gupta period established the basic Indian temple elements, a square sanctum and pillared porch, with a covered circumambulation path; later temples developed a shikhara.
Door-frame motifs of ganas, mithunas, vidyadharas and dvarapalas, with a deity emblem at the centre of the lintel.
Earliest Gupta temples at Sanchi (Temple 17), Tigawa and Eran; derived from rock-cut prototypes such as Cave-shrine 1 at Udaigiri near Sanchi.

Gupta temples with a rudimentary shikhara, the characteristic feature of North Indian temple architecture; the Deogarh temple is panchayatana with a subsidiary shrine in each corner on a wide platform.
